input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV gives Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years. That is a multi-year renewal we cannot opt out of at all — worse than the walk-away trigger (automatic multi-year renewals) and well short of the fallback (renewal exit on ≤60 days' notice, uplift ≤5%). There is also no cap on renewal pricing, which compounds the exposure. Subsections II and III of the same Article contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement, so the Licensor-option sentence is also internally inconsistent; the minimal fix conforms it to the preferred position (mutual written agreement, 12-month renewal periods) and adds a CPI/3% uplift cap.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals and a capped price uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year renewal exercisable at the Licensor's sole option; our playbook requires renewal only by mutual written agreement (or 12-month renewals we can exit on 30 days' notice), consistent with subsections II and III of this Article. We have also capped any renewal price increase at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: Thereafter, this Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties for successive renewal periods of twelve (12) months each, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and three percent (3%).
